 Northern Illinois Food Bank, VanVleet Foundation distribute 1,700 Holiday Meals
 By Bill Dwyer for Chronicle Media — November 18, 2026 
 Lashonda Sullivan, Neighborhood Market specialist at the Northern Illinois Food Bank
joins volunteer Jenny McIlhone for a turkey distribution at Sunday’s Holiday Boxes
event at the Northern Illinois Food Bank’s Neighborhood Market. (Provided photo)
 The Northern Illinois Food Bank and the VanVleet Family Foundation are both old hands at helping people have a better holiday through the gift of nourishing, tasty food.
 On Sunday, Nov. 15, the two organizations joined forces to give away 1,700 Holiday Boxes to folks in Rockford. The boxes, which contained a turkey and all the fixings to go into preparing a traditional holiday meal for six to eight people, were distributed at the drive-thru distribution at Northern Illinois Food Bank’s Neighborhood Market, 1397 Sandy Hollow Road in Rockford.
 The boxes each contained approximately 15 pounds of shelf-stable food, including stuffing, turkey gravy, whole kernel corn, green beans, dry pinto beans, dry potatoes, cream of mushroom soup, white rice, canned fruit in juice, cranberry sauce, hot cocoa and dessert mix.
 Organizers say that while the main goal is to enjoy a satisfying holiday meal “with dignity while stretching household food budgets,” they also want to assure that people also learn about ongoing food assistance available throughout the year.
 “While our location has changed and we’ve moved to a drive-thru format, this year it’s about more than a Thanksgiving meal,” said Sue Danforth, president and co-founder of the VanVleet Family Foundation, along with Houston Rockets basketball player Fred VanVleet.
 “Our partnership with Northern Illinois Food Bank helps connect families to food resources all year long,” Danforth said.
 “We are grateful to the VanVleet Family Foundation and all of the
 community partners who are helping provide holiday meals and support for Rockford families,” said Julie Yurko, president and CEO of Northern Illinois Food Bank. “Food brings people together, especially during the holidays.”
 Yurko said a key goal of the food bank, beyond feeding people, is to provide education and information regarding resources available to people they refer to as “neighbors.”
 “Together, we’re making sure neighbors have food for today and connections to resources that can help throughout the year, because hunger doesn’t end after the holidays,” Yurko said. “Families will be able to connect with the Neighborhood Market year-round.”
 Danforth noted that VanVleet and the Northern Illinois Food Bank are part of a much larger circle of caring and giving.
 “Thanks to our amazing partners, Northern Illinois Food Bank, Pro Restoration, Hard Rock Casino Rockford, NBPA Foundation PLYRS UNTD, Alpine Inn, Rockford IceHogs, United Way, and GE Appliance,” she said.
 Additional 2026 Holiday Meal Box program sponsors include Tate & Lyle, Abbott, Jewel-Osco, Kubota Engine America, Nicor Gas, Prinova, and Winland Foods, along with volunteers and community supporters who help the Food Bank bring holiday meals to neighbors across Northern Illinois.
 The synergy between all those organizations, Yurko said, enables them “to reach even more families this Thanksgiving.”
 The VanVleet Family Foundation’s partnership with the NIFB is part of a plan to expand its 10-year-old organization’s reach. They organized their first Turkey Drive in 2016, and over the past decade it has provided more than 9,000 meals to the community of Rockford.
 Rockford native Fred VanVleet’s athletic career is one of dedication and perseverance. The Auburn High School prep star and two-time Missouri Valley Conference Larry Bird Player of the Year at Wichita State University was not selected in the 2016 NBA draft.
 Undaunted, VanVleet stayed true to his personal motto, “Bet on Yourself,” and signed a summer league contract with the Toronto Raptors. He eventually secured a multiyear deal with the team, and in 2019, he helped the Raptors win the NBA Championship over the defending champion Golden State Warriors.
 In 2022, VanVleet’s perseverance and work ethic paid off in historic fashion when he was named an NBA All-Star, one of only four undrafted players in league history to earn the honor. The next year, he made more history when he became the highest-paid undrafted player in NBA history, signing with his current team, the Houston Rockets.
 Off the court, VanVleet’s impact continues through The VanVleet Family Foundation, which provides resources for those in need, including school supplies, clothing, food, and educational programs.
 Sunday’s distribution was part of Northern Illinois Food Bank’s 27th annual Holiday Meal Box program, which will provide a total of 50,000 Holiday Meal Boxes to families across Northern Illinois this season.
 A member of Feeding America, the food bank, now in its 40th year with more than 1,000 volunteers, partners with more than 900 food pantries, soup kitchens, shelters, and youth and senior feeding programs to provide 320,000 meals a day in 13 counties, with their trademark “dignity, equity, and convenience.”
